grammar.name: Imperfetto: forms
grammar.scope: regular forms of all three conjugations; irregular essere, fare, dire, bere; quando ero piccolo/a

chapters.a_plot: The tin box from the wall: Chiara opens it and finds photos of her mother as a young woman on this very street. Franco tells stories of 'when you were little'.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia's boxes appear at Franco's door. She is 'just leaving a few things' there.
chapters.arc: Season premiere: the Anna arc and the Lucia-moves-in arc begin. Back to school: Emma in terza, Leo in quarta.

grammar.name: Imperfetto for description
grammar.scope: describing people, places, weather, age, time and feelings in the past (era, aveva, c'era, c'erano, faceva freddo)

chapters.theme: The neighbourhood in the past; urban change
chapters.a_plot: Ornella shows Leo and Ben her photo albums: Via dei Tigli in 1962, when there were fields, a farmhouse and only three houses. The Bar Tigli was Gino's dream.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto wants to write a 'history of the street' for the committee newsletter and asks Ornella for an interview. She refuses and gives it to Ben instead.
chapters.runner: Leo can't believe there were no phones.

grammar.name: Imperfetto for habits and repeated actions
grammar.scope: di solito, ogni giorno/estate, sempre, spesso + imperfetto; contrast with present habits

chapters.theme: School then and now; summers and family habits
chapters.a_plot: Chiara and Matteo compete over who remembers their childhood summers 'right': Liguria every August, their mother's rules, their father's car.
chapters.b_plot: Franco visits Leo's school for 'grandparents' day' and tells the class what school was like in 1960.

grammar.name: Imperfetto vs passato prossimo
grammar.scope: background (imperfetto) vs events (passato prossimo); one-time vs habitual; typical signal words

chapters.theme: Love stories, meeting, dating in the past
chapters.a_plot: Emma interviews Franco for a school assignment: 'How did you meet Nonna Anna?' The story of a young tram driver and a passenger who always missed her stop.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia and Matteo tell Ben how they met (at the pharmacy, Matteo pretending to be sick). They remember it completely differently.
chapters.arc: Anna arc: Franco and Anna's story is told for the first time.

grammar.name: Mentre; imperfetto progressive
grammar.scope: mentre + imperfetto; stavo + gerund; interrupted actions (mentre cucinavo, è arrivato...)

chapters.a_plot: Leo falls off Tommaso's skateboard and breaks his arm. At the emergency room, every adult tells the doctor what they were doing when it happened.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto blames Tommaso; Ben defends him. Emma sees her father standing up for her boyfriend.

grammar.name: Sapere and conoscere in past tenses
grammar.scope: sapevo (knew) vs ho saputo (found out); conoscevo (knew) vs ho conosciuto (met); potevo/volevo vs ho potuto/voluto

chapters.a_plot: Roberto confronts Ben: 'Lei lo sapeva?' about Emma and Tommaso. Ben did know. Chiara didn't.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara finds letters from Anna in the tin box that mention 'L.' Is it Lucia? Did her mother know Lucia?
chapters.runner: Leo knew everything first, as always.

grammar.name: Informal imperative (tu)
grammar.scope: affirmative tu imperative for -are/-ere/-ire; irregular va', fa', da', di', sta'; recipe language

chapters.a_plot: Chiara finds Anna's handwritten recipe notebook. She tries to cook her mother's lasagne with Lucia reading the instructions.
chapters.b_plot: Ben teaches Leo (one-handed, in plaster) to cook pancakes: 'Mescola! No, piano!'

grammar.name: Negative imperative; voi imperative
grammar.scope: non + infinitive (tu); voi forms; noi (let's) forms; common commands for groups

chapters.a_plot: Ben's parents Doug and Linda arrive from Ohio for two weeks. For the first time Ben is the one who speaks Italian, and he gives everyone instructions.
chapters.b_plot: Franco prepares to meet 'the Americans' seriously: a suit, and a speech in English he has been practising alone.

grammar.name: Imperative with pronouns
grammar.scope: pronouns attached to tu/noi/voi imperatives (dimmi, fallo, andiamoci, seguitemi); doubling with monosyllabic forms (fammi, dammi, stammi)

chapters.a_plot: Ben is the family tour guide in Milan: the Duomo, the Galleria, the Castello. Linda wants to shop, Doug wants a real coffee (American), and Ben gets them lost.
chapters.b_plot: Franco and Doug, alone for the day with no common language, spend it in the orto and at the bocce court. They get along perfectly.

grammar.name: Formal imperative (Lei)
grammar.scope: Lei imperative forms (prenda, scusi, venga, si accomodi, mi dica); pronoun position before formal imperatives

chapters.a_plot: Ben books a fancy restaurant in Milan for his parents' anniversary. The waiter is very formal and Ben must translate every formal instruction.
chapters.b_plot: Emma introduces Tommaso to her American grandparents before he's been properly introduced to her Italian ones. Chiara is offended.
chapters.runner: Doug tips 30%; the waiter is confused.

grammar.name: Combined pronouns
grammar.scope: me lo, te la, glielo, gliela, ce ne, ve li; with passato prossimo; with infinitives and imperatives

chapters.a_plot: Doug and Linda's last day. Everyone gives them gifts, too many for the suitcase. Franco gives Doug his old tram driver's cap.
chapters.b_plot: At the airport Linda tells Ben she's never seen him so happy. Ben is surprised to realise it's true.
chapters.arc: End of Ben's parents' visit. Franco–Doug friendship.

grammar.name: Conditional for politeness and wishes
grammar.scope: vorrei, potrei, potresti, dovresti, mi piacerebbe, sarebbe; regular conditional forms as a first look

chapters.theme: Shopping for a baby; asking for help politely
chapters.a_plot: Matteo and Nadia go shopping for the baby with an 'advisor' each: Samira and Lucia. Every suggestion is polite and every suggestion is a war.
chapters.b_plot: Ben would like Franco to teach him bocce seriously. Franco would like Ben to stop asking.
chapters.runner: Ornella knits something every episode; nobody knows what it is.

grammar.name: Stare per + infinitive
grammar.scope: stare per (be about to); contrast with stare + gerund; present and imperfetto (stavo per uscire quando...)

chapters.a_plot: Nadia goes into labour on Christmas Eve day, during a train strike and a snowstorm. Everyone is about to do something useful, and nobody does.
chapters.b_plot: Ben drives, Franco gives directions, Samira and Lucia argue in the back seat, and Matteo is still at the bar.

grammar.name: Relative pronouns che and cui
grammar.scope: che as subject/object; preposition + cui; la persona che, il motivo per cui, la casa in cui

chapters.theme: Birth, family, names and their meaning
chapters.a_plot: The baby is born: a girl. In the waiting room, the family argues about names, and then Nadia and Matteo announce 'Anna Yasmin'. Franco has to leave the room.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara holds the baby and tells her about the grandmother 'after whom you are named', the woman who...
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: Anna Yasmin Ferri Benali is born.

grammar.name: Diminutives and augmentatives
grammar.scope: -ino, -etto, -ello (small/affectionate); -one (big); -accio (bad); common lexicalised forms (il telefonino, il fratellino)

chapters.a_plot: Christmas with a newborn at Franco's. Lucia speaks only in diminutives, and Leo counts them all.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo, sleepless, tries to run the bar and makes a 'caffettino' disaster. Ben covers the morning shift alone for a week.
chapters.runner: Ornella finally reveals what she has been knitting: a tiny blanket.

grammar.name: Possessive pronouns
grammar.scope: il mio, la tua, i suoi, le nostre as pronouns; di chi è?; è mio vs è il mio; i miei (my parents)

chapters.theme: Belongings, sharing a home, moving in
chapters.a_plot: Lucia officially moves in with Franco. Whose armchair? Whose plates? Anna's things are still everywhere. Chiara has to decide what to keep.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Leo fight over 'mine' and 'yours' after the renovation; the new room is 'ours'.
chapters.arc: Lucia moves in. Chiara starts to let go.

grammar.name: Ci and ne with verbs
grammar.scope: pensarci, crederci, tenerci, riuscirci, contarci; parlarne, pensarne (che ne pensi?), andarsene as a preview

chapters.a_plot: 'Ci penso io': why Chiara can't stop taking care of everyone: work, Franco, Ben, and now baby Anna. She cracks.
chapters.b_plot: Emma asks Ben: 'Che ne pensi di Tommaso?' Ben's honest answer surprises them both.

grammar.name: Basic connectors
grammar.scope: perché, quindi, però, allora, siccome, infatti, invece, mentre, anche se, prima/poi/alla fine; linking a story or letter

chapters.a_plot: At the bottom of the tin box, a sealed letter: 'Per Chiara.' Anna wrote it before she died. Chiara reads it alone, then to Franco.
chapters.b_plot: The letter mentions 'L.': Anna and Lucia were friends at the dance class. Anna had asked Lucia to 'keep an eye on Franco'.
chapters.arc: TENTPOLE: Anna's letter. The Lucia mystery is resolved.

grammar.name: Irregular plurals (the body and more)
grammar.scope: il braccio → le braccia, il ginocchio → le ginocchia, la mano → le mani, l'uovo → le uova, il dito → le dita; invariable nouns (il film, la città)

chapters.theme: The body, the doctor, getting older
chapters.a_plot: Franco's knees hurt, but he refuses to see a doctor. Lucia, Chiara and Nadia (a pharmacist) form an alliance to get him there.
chapters.b_plot: Leo's plaster comes off; he shows his arm to everyone.
chapters.runner: Franco blames the knees on Ben's bocce technique.

grammar.name: Expressions with fare
grammar.scope: fare finta di, fare la spesa, fare due passi, fare una sorpresa, fare attenzione, fare la fila, fare bella figura / brutta figura

chapters.a_plot: Chiara's boss Marchetti and his wife come to dinner in Borgoverde. Chiara wants to 'fare bella figura'. Every relative makes a brutta figura.
chapters.b_plot: Tommaso pretends to like the jazz Emma likes; Emma pretends to like skating.
chapters.runner: Ben's rule list from S2 gains a new entry: 'la bella figura'.

grammar.name: Andare/venire, portare/prendere
grammar.scope: andare vs venire depending on the speaker's position; portare vs prendere; tornare, passare, accompagnare; volerci vs metterci

chapters.a_plot: A national train strike. Chiara needs to get to Milan for a crucial meeting; Emma to Monza for an exam. Ben becomes the family's taxi.
chapters.b_plot: Franco, the retired tram driver, has strong opinions on strikes. He talks about the 1970s, and the whole bar listens.
chapters.runner: 'Vengo io!' 'No, vado io!' Who is coming and who is going?

grammar.name: Large numbers, percentages, fractions, money
grammar.scope: mille, un milione; percentages; fractions (un terzo, la metà); money language (spendere, risparmiare, prestare, il debito)

chapters.a_plot: The bar's accounts: Nadia, on maternity leave, looks at them and finds the old loan from Franco. The unspoken debt is finally spoken.
chapters.b_plot: Ben and Chiara do the family budget after the renovation. The numbers are frightening, and the conversation is honest.
chapters.arc: Matteo–Franco: the debt is out in the open.

grammar.name: Exclamations and interjections
grammar.scope: che + adjective/noun (che bello!, che peccato!); come/quanto + verb!; interjections (magari!, figurati!, accidenti!, dai!, boh, uffa)

chapters.a_plot: Carnevale again: the family goes to the Carnevale parade in Milan. It's a day of big reactions, including Franco dressed as a tram.
chapters.b_plot: Leo and Pietro write a comic in Italian full of exclamations; Maestra Paola loves it.
chapters.runner: Uffa! is Emma's word of the week.

grammar.name: Narrating in the past: review
grammar.scope: imperfetto + passato prossimo in extended narrative; time sequencing (prima, poi, dopo, alla fine); telling a story aloud

chapters.a_plot: Franco secretly asks Ben for help: he wants to propose to Lucia, and he wants to do it 'like in a story'. Ben helps him plan it.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Tommaso tell the story of how they got together at a class assembly, each in their own version.
chapters.arc: Proposal set-up. Anna's ring (S2E7) is found.

grammar.name: A2 review
grammar.scope: Consolidation of A2: past narration (passato prossimo/imperfetto), all pronouns, imperative, polite conditional, comparisons

chapters.a_plot: At Lucia's Valentine's dance evening, Franco stops the music and gets down on one (painful) knee. Chiara shouts 'Sì!' before Lucia does.
chapters.b_plot: Ben and Chiara, both exhausted, dance for the first time in years.
chapters.arc: SEASON FINALE: the proposal. End of A2.
